issues.issue: The detailed list has an exact 'water charges' category, and that is what the line is labelled.

The extractor's own review says this holds Lease Income 11,000 (p3), and the budget equals the lease exactly. The dominant part is rental income, so it should be charges for services/fees / rentals with a review note, not other.

All budget-schedule expenditure lines were left out 'to avoid double counting' with the Schedules of Expenses (pp8-9). But those schedules cover only Directors/Field/General and Office operating expenses (1,069,589). Capital outlay and debt service appear nowhere else in the JSON, so leaving them out drops 2,137,100 of printed spending instead of avoiding a double count.

This cash-basis operating line overlaps the more detailed accrual Schedules of Expenses, so leaving it out is defensible. It isn't recorded anywhere, and the detail mixes cash-basis revenue with accrual expenses.

The budget schedule (p7) shows these receipts are mostly 'Special Emergency Assessment' 1,165,336 plus Water Charges 56,726. The detail calls the same money special assessments, so the receipts category and the detail category don't match. The label supports charges, so this is a judgment call.

This entity is mainly an irrigation district (canal, dam, lateral rehab, groundwater recharge). natural resources/conservation could be the better function for every line. utilities is defensible under the public power district rule.
